why: Indexation is not stalled, it is decaying: 6 of 25 on 2026-10-22 -> 5 of 22 on 2026-10-28 -> 3 of 21 on 2026-10-29. The three URLs Google dropped in seven days were all last crawled in August (08-16, 08-17, 08-17), all were live 200 pages in sitemap.xml on the day they dropped, and the two still inspectable today show a matching canonical, so this is not a discovery, canonical or robots defect: Google crawled them once in August and is now withdrawing them. Stage: crawled, declined, then de-indexed. The only in-repo action left untested was removing surface, and we did that (25 -> 22 -> 21) while the count still fell. Test: the sitemap-contraction bar was 8 of 22 by 2026-11-10 with <=5/22 closing it failed; at 3/21 twelve days early that bar is already met, so it is closed failed today rather than after another five cycles of churn. If indexed exceeds 3 before a single URL is added or removed, the cause was never our on-page work.

The impression and click collapse is the same event, not noise. The week to 2026-10-19 produced 45 impressions and 14 clicks and its page table returned 11 URLs (74 impressions byPage, 29 of them on the ten non-homepage URLs, at positions 2-6, all on the brand family: 'btc500' 3/16, 'btc 500', 'bitcoin 500', 'bit 500', 'bitcoin plus 500'); the week to 2026-10-26 produced 10 impressions and 1 click on one URL. Eight consecutive 7-day readings each lower than the last (clicks 14,10,9,8,8,7,5,1; impressions 45,37,31,28,26,21,16,10) is a 1-in-128 run if the moves were random, so the growth log's 'at this base every movement is noise' is the wrong read this week. Stage: indexed -> not served, as Google withdrew the URL set and then de-indexed two of the pages that carried it. Test: on 2026-11-05, if the 7-day page table is still 1 row while indexed is <=3, the site is in a de-indexing spiral and no on-page change can be read until a link arrives.

Non-brand is not stalled at a low number, it is absent. In the 28 days to 2026-10-26, all 5 named queries contain the brand - btc500 4/40, btc 500 0/1, bitcoin 500 0/3, bit 500 0/1, bitcoin plus 500 0/2 - so nothing in that table is a query a stranger would type without already looking for us by name; the four variants the collector's narrow /btc 500/ regex would call non-brand carry 6 impressions and 0 clicks. In the 90 days to 2026-10-24 there are 723 non-brand impressions and 1 click. 61% of all 90-day impressions (2,067 of 3,378) came from one dated news page, /articles/bitcoin-week-ahead, which produced 1 click and which 2c7f981 noindexed on 2026-10-22; its demand was August-dated and had already decayed out of the 7-day window by 10-19, so the noindex did not cause this week's fall, but nothing replaced it either: the durable 500-day set produces 10 impressions and 1 brand click a week. Stage: indexed, but the pages that answer the query are not served - the four cluster queries sit at 8.00-15.29 with 28 impressions and 0 clicks on declined URLs. Test: the H1 change of 2026-10-29 is read on 2026-11-08 (not 11-04: GSC lags ~3 days, so the old date left only ~3 days of post-change data). If the cluster is absent from both the 7-day and 28-day query tables that day, the cluster has no demand at this authority and the answer belongs on no page until the site has links.

Input and output do not just fail to balance, they now point in opposite directions. Four cycles ran (3 shipped + 1 archive-only, 0 failures) and all four previous mandates were executed and verified in production: the GSC collector reconciles, /articles/strongest-hands 308s to /articles and the sitemap is 21, the homepage H1 reads '500 days before the next Bitcoin halving is 28 November 2026' live, and STATUS.md matches the referral evidence. Output: indexed 6 -> 3, weekly clicks 14 -> 1, weekly impressions 45 -> 10, non-brand 0, external referral sources 0. That is not a compliance failure, it is proof that the mandate menu and the backlog are both choosing in-repo work on a site Google has declined 18 of 21 URLs on. When four well-executed cycles make the gate metric worse, the next four must not be more of the same.

Distribution is still zero and the loop is now blocked at the human, not at preparation. Referrals 7d are github.com 9 (2 users, our own repository per STATUS.md) and 0 from every other source - not one external site is visibly referring sessions; 4 asks handed over since 2026-10-27 and 0 sent. Stage: no links. The one ask that survives is the GitHub listing, because github.com is the only channel where the owner demonstrably acts (daily commits, all 9 recorded referral sessions), and it is small enough to do in two minutes. Test: if it is still sent: no on 2026-11-11 with 0 bitcoin-only.com sessions, the bottleneck is the owner's five minutes and no review can change it - the honest consequence is to stop issuing asks and stop publishing until somebody acts.

The measurement layer is no longer the excuse. The 2026-10-28 review read the 10-rows-to-1-row collapse as a broken report; it was byProperty vs byPage, and the fix now prints both, labels every derived field with its window and keeps the previous file on refusal. That correction makes this week's verdict harder, not easier: the decline survives reconciliation. The one remaining measurement caveat is that the runner's only positive outcome signal is a 9-session self-referral from github.com, so '1 green signal' overstates the week - with that signal read honestly, there are zero.

The only positive outcome signal this week is 9 sessions from 2 users via github.com - the owner's own repo. Why does the rule count that as an improvement, and what would the week look like with it excluded?

Four asks handed over since 2026-10-27, zero sent, zero sessions from every asked channel. Is the blocker the ask text, or is nobody at the keyboard - and if it is the second, what is a daily review for?

The site is four months old, has 3 indexed URLs, 0 external referral sources and 1 click a week. Is the goal still a recognised research site, or should the cycle stop publishing until one external link exists?

owner_asks.content:
Title: Add BTC500 - Bitcoin halving 500-day window dashboard (Bitcoin-only, no altcoins)

Suggestion: BTC500 (https://btc500.net) for Explorers & Dashboards.

What it is: a Bitcoin-only research site built on one fixed rule - buy 500 days before each halving, sell 500 days after. Four completed windows (2012, 2016, 2020, 2024) with entry, halving and exit closes, the lowest close inside each window and the date it happened, and what moving the entry 30, 60 or 120 days did at the same exit. The next T-500 date, 28 November 2026, is on the homepage.

No altcoins, no accounts, no ads. Every number is also served as JSON for anyone who wants to chart it: https://btc500.net/data/500-day-cycles.json
